title: Class Introduction

sections.title: Pragmatic Electrical Diagnostics
sections.text: Why are we doing this and what do you want to take away from this class?

sections.title: Learning Objectives
sections.text: Build a solid foundation of electrical problem solving. Leave this class with a simplified, repeatable diagnostic method that gets you solutions to even those difficult intermittent failures. Participate in hands-on labs. Analyze, evaluate, and create your own methods within the 7-step diagnostic process.

sections.title: Examples
sections.text: Service Manual Low Voltage Testing. Diagnostic Guide Starting System Electrical Concern. No Backup Alarm. Diagnosing a Blown Fuse.

sections.title: First Principals
sections.text: Follow the 7-Step procedure and build simple diagnostic plans using schematics to make every failure a series circuit. Use Ohm's Law to solve for current. Source, path, and load. Voltage-drop. The voltmeter is your primary weapon.

sections.title: Be careful when you relate electricity to hydraulics
sections.text: Current, Resistance, Voltage compared to Flow, Restriction, Pressure.

sections.title: Battery Circuits
sections.text: Any circuit directly powered by the machine battery. Unfused high current starting and charging circuits, fused circuits, and circuits involving relays. Voltage-drop testing.

sections.title: Snap Circuits
sections.text: Explore basic electrical theories before working with powered Bobcat components. Don't short the battery. Series and parallel circuits.

sections.title: Trainer Kit
sections.text: Built to resemble Bobcat components. 12-volt power supply acts as the machine battery. Glow plugs get hot.

sections.title: Schematic
sections.text: Trainer Kit Schematic. Experiment with the kit. Make all the circuits work. Lights dim and bright. Pull/hold solenoid. HVAC fan. Glow plug temperature.

title: Solder Projects

sections.title: Solder versus crimp repairs
sections.text: Solder projects for repairs kept small, or when the correct terminal isn't available. Soldering is about controlling heat. Tin the solder iron. Pre-heat with a heat gun. Crimp repairs are very reliable and often superior.

sections.title: Test Leads
sections.text: 4-Foot silicone wire red and black leads. Male 4mm banana plugs. Plug boots with flex relief slots. Strip just enough insulation. Avoid twisting conductors. Solder all 4 plugs.

sections.title: High-Current Test Light
sections.text: Handle, magnet, bolt and nut, crimp and seal eyelet, insulated P-clamp, ground wire, 1156 bulbs and bulb holders, female 4mm banana jacks.

sections.title: Assemble the bulb holder
sections.text: Bulb holders wired in parallel. Bulbs ground through the bulb holder. Positive wires soldered to a single 4mm female banana socket.

sections.title: Assemble the ground wire
sections.text: Solder the single ground wire to a 4mm female socket. Crimp the number 8 eyelet with the insulated die. Heat the eyelet to seal.

sections.title: Assemble Bulb Holders
sections.text: Pass the 8x32 screw through the handle. Install both bulb holders, the ground wire eyelet, and 8x32 nut.

sections.title: Assemble Magnet and P-Clamp
sections.text: Insert threaded post of magnet through second hole. Secure P-clamp around all three wires. Install P-clamp, washer, lock washer, and nut.

title: Current

sections.title: Current Lab Learning Objectives
sections.text: Three basic requirements for every circuit. Kirchhoff's Current Law. Voltage-drop. How can I narrow possible failures when a fuse blows. Internal DVOM ammeter and the clamp-style meter.

sections.title: 3 Requirements for Current Flow
sections.text: Source, load, and path. Batteries and Alternators. Wire Harness. Lights, Solenoids, Motors. Resistance of the circuit load determines current flow. A complete path is required.

sections.title: Electrostatic Force
sections.text: Current is as predictable as gravity. Electrostatic force is one of the four fundamental forces of nature. Opposite charges attract and like charges repel.

sections.title: Current Has a Direction
sections.text: Electron flow or Conventional flow. AC and DC. Alternating current changes direction. Conventional current flow is from positive to negative.

sections.title: DVOM Current Measured with Your Internal Ammeter
sections.text: Use the correct jacks in your meter. Meter must be in series with the circuit. Be careful with your meter's fuse. Amps, milliamps, micro-amps.

sections.title: Measuring Current Series Ammeter
sections.text: Break the circuit to insert the meter. Always in series with the load. Use the current jacks of my meter.

sections.title: Current and Magnetic Fields
sections.text: Current flow through a conductor creates a magnetic field. A conductor traveling through a magnetic field will have current generated in it.

sections.title: Measuring Current Clamp Meter
sections.text: No need to open a circuit to test current with a clamp style ammeter. Clamp measures the magnetic field around the conductor. Zero the clamp.

title: Resistance

sections.title: Learning Objectives
sections.text: How to read your ohmmeter. The ohmmeter is almost never the best tool. Everything has resistance. Ohm's Law series and parallel resistance. Resistance is the load in our circuit.

sections.title: Source Load Path
sections.text: Voltage comes from the source. Circuit wires make up the path. Resistance is the load. Resistance is opposition to current flow. In a series circuit all resistance adds together.

sections.title: Ohm's Law
sections.text: Current equals Volts over Ohms. Resistance is indirectly related to current. As resistance goes up, current decreases.

sections.title: Conductors and Insulators
sections.text: Materials with little resistance are conductors: copper, aluminum, steel. Materials with lots of resistance are insulators: glass, rubber, vinyl. A short-to-ground has basically no resistance.

sections.title: Typical Resistance Readings
sections.text: Save your ohmmeter for circuit testing scenarios. Light bulb, piece of wire, switch, connector. Resistance affected by temperature, length, diameter, and material composition.

sections.title: Reading the Meter
sections.text: Meter settings: resistance ohms omega symbol, continuity beeper, diode test. Meter counts and range changes. OL means open loop or overload, infinite resistance.
